category: Industry Toolsets, AutoCAD LT, Web & Mobile
description: The specialized toolsets included with an AutoCAD subscription (Architecture, MEP, Electrical, Mechanical, Map 3D, Plant 3D, Raster Design) with their key commands, plus the capabilities and limits of AutoCAD LT, the AutoCAD web app and the mobile app. Toolsets are installed and launched as separate products on top of AutoCAD for Windows and add their own object types, which plain AutoCAD shows through object enablers or proxies.

tools.name: AutoCAD Architecture toolset
tools.description: Architectural design and documentation toolset built on AutoCAD with intelligent AEC objects (walls, doors, windows, stairs, roofs, slabs, spaces), styles, a display system, schedules and the Project Navigator for building projects. Drawings created with it contain AEC objects that plain AutoCAD shows through object enablers.
tools.usage:
Start the 'AutoCAD Architecture 2025' shortcut (it runs acad.exe with a /product switch selecting the toolset)
Key commands: WALLADD, DOORADD, WINDOWADD, SPACEADD, SCHEDULEADD, STYLEMANAGER

parameters.name: AEC objects
parameters.description: Style-driven parametric building elements with display representations per view.

parameters.name: Project Navigator
parameters.description: Manages constructs, views and sheets of a building project.

parameters.name: EXPORTTOAUTOCAD
parameters.description: Creates a copy with AEC objects exploded to plain AutoCAD geometry for consultants.

tools.example:
WALLADD  (draw walls)
DOORADD  (insert doors into walls)
SPACEADD (add spaces)
SCHEDULEADD (door schedule)
EXPORTTOAUTOCAD (issue a plain DWG)
tools.notes: AEC objects can be automated through the AutoCAD Architecture .NET/COM API (AecBaseMgd, AecArchMgd). Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: WALLADD
tools.description: AutoCAD Architecture command that adds wall objects of the current (or last used) wall style by picking start and end points, with width, height, justification and baseline offset set in the Properties palette. Walls clean up automatically at intersections and host doors and windows.
tools.usage:
WALLADD
Specify start point of wall (style, width, base height and justification from the Properties palette or command options)
Specify end point of wall ... Enter to finish

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Wall style defining components, materials and display.

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: Wall dimensions.

parameters.name: Justify
parameters.description: Left, Center, Right or Baseline.

tools.notes: WALLCLEANUPI fixes L and T intersections; WALLSTYLEEDIT edits the style of a selected wall.

tools.name: DOORADD
tools.description: AutoCAD Architecture command that inserts door objects of the chosen door style into walls, anchoring them so they move with the wall and cut an opening. Position can be unconstrained, offset from wall ends or centered, and size comes from the style's standard sizes.
tools.usage:
DOORADD
Select wall, grid assembly or RETURN
Specify insertion point (style, size and position-along-wall options in the Properties palette)

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Door style (single, double, sliding ...).

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: Door size; standard sizes defined by the style.

parameters.name: Position along wall
parameters.description: Unconstrained, offset or centered placement.

tools.example:
DOORADD
<pick wall>
<pick insertion point>
; use the Properties palette to set style 'Hinged - Single' and 900 x 2100
tools.notes: WINDOWADD works the same way for windows; openings are updated when the wall changes.

tools.name: WINDOWADD
tools.description: AutoCAD Architecture command that adds window objects of the chosen window style into walls (anchored) or freestanding, with size, sill height and positioning options similar to DOORADD.
tools.usage:
WINDOWADD
Select wall, grid assembly or RETURN
Specify insertion point or options

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Window style (casement, double-hung, fixed ...).

parameters.name: Width / Height / Sill height
parameters.description: Size and vertical position.

tools.example:
WINDOWADD
<pick wall>
<pick position along wall>
tools.notes: Window and door schedules read their data from these objects and their property sets.

tools.name: SPACEADD
tools.description: AutoCAD Architecture command that adds a space object (room area with name, floor area and height data) of the current space style, drawn or generated from bounding walls. Spaces drive area calculations, room tags and schedules.
tools.usage:
SPACEADD
Generate from bounding objects, insert a rectangle, or draw a polygon (options in the Properties palette)

parameters.name: Style / Name
parameters.description: Space style and room name.

parameters.name: Create type
parameters.description: Insert, Rectangle, Polygon or Generate (from walls).

tools.example:
SPACEADD
<Generate: pick inside a room bounded by walls>
tools.notes: Associative spaces update when bounding walls move; non-associative spaces must be edited manually.

tools.name: SCHEDULEADD
tools.description: AutoCAD Architecture command that adds a schedule table listing information (from property sets) about selected objects such as doors, windows or spaces, optionally updating automatically when objects change.
tools.usage:
SCHEDULEADD
Select objects
Upper left corner of table

parameters.name: Schedule style
parameters.description: Defines columns, property sets and formatting.

parameters.name: Update automatically
parameters.description: Keeps the table in sync with the model.

tools.example:
SCHEDULEADD
<select all doors>
<pick table location>
tools.notes: SCHEDULETAG adds tags that feed the schedule; property set definitions supply the data.

tools.name: STYLEMANAGER
tools.description: Opens the AutoCAD Architecture/MEP Style Manager for creating, editing, copying and purging the styles that define AEC objects (wall, door, window, space, schedule, MEP part styles) across drawings.
tools.usage: STYLEMANAGER

parameters.name: drawings
parameters.description: Open drawings and style libraries shown side by side for copying styles.

tools.example:
STYLEMANAGER
<drag wall styles from the office library drawing into the current drawing>
tools.notes: Different from STYLESMANAGER, which opens the plot-styles folder in plain AutoCAD.

tools.name: AutoCAD MEP toolset
tools.description: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing design toolset built on AutoCAD Architecture: duct, pipe, cable tray and conduit runs with catalog-based parts, devices and panels, systems, connectivity and MEP schedules.
tools.usage:
Start the 'AutoCAD MEP 2025' shortcut
Key commands: DUCTADD, PIPEADD, CABLETRAYADD, CONDUITADD, DEVICEADD

parameters.name: parts catalogs
parameters.description: Fittings and equipment defined in content catalogs.

parameters.name: systems
parameters.description: Supply air, domestic cold water, power, etc. controlling layers and display.

tools.example: DUCTADD (route supply duct) -> PIPEADD (route hydronic piping) -> DEVICEADD (receptacles) -> CONDUITADD
tools.notes: Includes all AutoCAD Architecture functionality. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: DUCTADD
tools.description: AutoCAD MEP command that adds duct runs of a chosen system, shape and size, inserting fittings (elbows, tees, transitions) automatically according to the routing preferences as points are picked.
tools.usage:
DUCTADD
Specify start point (set System, Shape, Width/Height or Diameter, Elevation in the Properties palette)
Specify next point ...

parameters.name: System
parameters.description: Duct system (e.g. Supply - Low Pressure).

parameters.name: Shape / Size
parameters.description: Rectangular, round or oval with dimensions.

parameters.name: Routing preference
parameters.description: Fittings used at bends and branches.

tools.example:
DUCTADD
<pick start at AHU outlet>
<pick bend points>
<Enter>
tools.notes: Connecting to existing ducts or equipment connectors creates connected systems usable for analysis and schedules.

tools.name: PIPEADD
tools.description: AutoCAD MEP command that adds pipe runs of a chosen system, size and routing preference, placing fittings automatically, for plumbing and hydronic piping.
tools.usage:
PIPEADD
Specify start point (System, Nominal size, Routing preference, Elevation in the Properties palette)
Specify next point ...

parameters.name: System
parameters.description: Piping system (Domestic Cold Water, Hot Water Supply ...).

parameters.name: Nominal size
parameters.description: Pipe size from the catalog.

tools.example:
PIPEADD
<pick start at riser>
<route along corridor>
<Enter>
tools.notes: Sloped piping (drainage) is set with the slope options of the command.

tools.name: CABLETRAYADD
tools.description: AutoCAD MEP command that adds cable tray runs with width, height and system, inserting cable tray fittings at bends and branches.
tools.usage:
CABLETRAYADD
Specify start point / next points (System, Width, Height, Elevation in the Properties palette)

parameters.name: System
parameters.description: Cable tray system.

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: Tray size.

tools.example:
CABLETRAYADD
<pick start>
<pick end>
<Enter>
tools.notes: Cable trays and conduits are routing objects only; circuiting is done with devices and panels.

tools.name: CONDUITADD
tools.description: AutoCAD MEP command that adds conduit runs of a given system and nominal size, placing conduit fittings automatically.
tools.usage:
CONDUITADD
Specify start point / next points

parameters.name: System / Nominal size
parameters.description: Conduit system and diameter.

tools.example:
CONDUITADD
<pick from panel>
<pick to junction box>
<Enter>
tools.notes: Conduits can connect to cable trays and devices with conduit connectors.

tools.name: DEVICEADD
tools.description: AutoCAD MEP command that adds electrical devices (receptacles, switches, lights, sensors) from device styles, optionally attaching them to walls and assigning circuits.
tools.usage:
DEVICEADD
Select style, then insertion point (options for spacing along walls and circuit assignment)

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Device style with symbol and connectors.

parameters.name: Circuit
parameters.description: Assign to a panel circuit for load calculations.

tools.example:
DEVICEADD
<choose Duplex Receptacle style>
<pick points along the wall>
tools.notes: Circuit Manager reports loads per panel once devices are circuited.

tools.name: AutoCAD Electrical toolset
tools.description: Electrical controls design toolset for schematics and panel layouts: project-based drawing sets, intelligent component symbols (JIC, IEC and other standards), wires and wire numbering, cross-referencing, PLC I/O, terminal strips, catalog-based part data and automatic reports (BOM, wire lists, from/to).
tools.usage:
Start the 'AutoCAD Electrical 2025' shortcut
Key commands: AEPROJECT, AECOMPONENT, AEWIRE, AEWIRENO

parameters.name: project (.wdp)
parameters.description: Text file listing the drawings and settings of a project.

parameters.name: catalog database
parameters.description: Access/SQL database with manufacturer part numbers.

parameters.name: symbol libraries
parameters.description: Schematic and panel symbols with WD attributes.

tools.example: AEPROJECT (open project) -> AECOMPONENT (insert push button) -> AEWIRE (connect) -> AEWIRENO (number wires) -> reports
tools.notes: Toolset commands are unknown in plain AutoCAD; 'Unknown command AEPROJECT' usually means the drawing was opened in AutoCAD instead of the Electrical shortcut. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: AEPROJECT
tools.description: AutoCAD Electrical command that opens the Project Manager, where projects (.wdp) are created, opened and activated, drawings are added and ordered, and project-wide tasks (retag, update title blocks, reports) are run.
tools.usage: AEPROJECT

parameters.name: active project
parameters.description: Only one project is active; cross-references and reports use it.

tools.example:
AEPROJECT
<New Project... MachineX.wdp> <Add Drawings...>
tools.notes: Drawings must belong to the active project for cross-referencing and reporting to work.

tools.name: AECOMPONENT
tools.description: AutoCAD Electrical command that opens the icon menu of schematic symbols and inserts the selected component, tagging it automatically, breaking wires it is placed on and prompting for descriptions, catalog data and cross-references.
tools.usage:
AECOMPONENT
choose a symbol from the icon menu
Specify insertion point
Insert/Edit Component dialog

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Component tag generated from sheet/line reference or sequential format.

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.description: Manufacturer and part number lookup.

tools.example:
AECOMPONENT
<Push Buttons > Normally Open>
<pick on a rung>
<accept tag PB101, enter description START>
tools.notes: Components are blocks with specific attribute names; use the provided symbol builder to create custom symbols.

tools.name: AEWIRE
tools.description: AutoCAD Electrical command that inserts wires between component connection points on the current wire type layer, with automatic wire routing and connection to wire connection attributes.
tools.usage:
AEWIRE
Specify wire start (options include choosing the wire type and showing connection points)
Specify wire end ...

parameters.name: wire type
parameters.description: Layer-based wire type (color, size).

parameters.name: connections
parameters.description: Wires connect at component terminal attributes.

tools.example:
AEWIRE
<pick terminal of PB101>
<pick terminal of CR1>
tools.notes: Wires are lines on wire layers; do not draw them with LINE on other layers or connectivity is lost.

tools.name: AEWIRENO
tools.description: AutoCAD Electrical command that inserts or updates wire numbers on wire networks for the drawing or project, using sequential or line-reference-based formats defined in the project settings.
tools.usage:
AEWIRENO
Sequential / Reference-based options, Drawing-wide or Project-wide

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Wire number format from project/drawing properties.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Pick individually, drawing-wide or project-wide.

tools.example:
AEWIRENO
<Drawing-wide>
tools.notes: Fixed wire numbers are preserved when renumbering.

tools.name: AutoCAD Mechanical toolset
tools.description: Mechanical drafting toolset with standards-based parts content (fasteners, shafts, steel shapes), power dimensioning with fits and tolerances, hidden-line structure, balloons, parts lists and BOM, and machinery generators and calculators. Commands use the AM prefix.
tools.usage:
Start the 'AutoCAD Mechanical 2025' shortcut
Key commands: AMPOWERDIM, AMBALLOON, AMBOM, AMPARTREF

parameters.name: standards
parameters.description: ISO, ANSI, DIN, JIS, GB, BSI and CSN drafting standards.

parameters.name: content library
parameters.description: Standard parts and features.

tools.example: AMPARTREF (identify parts) -> AMBALLOON (balloon them) -> AMBOM (edit BOM) -> parts list
tools.notes: Mechanical objects display as proxies in plain AutoCAD unless the object enabler is installed. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: AMPOWERDIM
tools.description: AutoCAD Mechanical power-dimensioning command that creates linear, aligned, angular and other dimensions in one session, creating dimension styles on demand and letting you add tolerances and fits directly.
tools.usage:
AMPOWERDIM
Specify first extension line origin (or select an object), second origin, dimension line location; edit tolerance/fit in the Power Dimensioning dialog

parameters.name: tolerances / fits
parameters.description: Added in the Power Dimensioning dialog after placement.

tools.example:
AMPOWERDIM
<pick two points>
<place dimension>
<add fit H7 in the dialog>
tools.notes: Dimension styles are managed by the drafting standard; editing them manually may be overwritten.

tools.name: AMBALLOON
tools.description: AutoCAD Mechanical command that creates and places balloons referencing part references in the bill of materials, with auto, one-by-one and collect options.
tools.usage:
AMBALLOON
Select part/assembly or choose an option (Autoballoon, Collect, One, Manual, Renumber, ...)

parameters.name: Autoballoon
parameters.description: Balloons many parts at once with alignment.

parameters.name: Renumber
parameters.description: Renumbers items in the BOM.

tools.example:
AMBALLOON
A
<select parts>
<pick alignment line>
tools.notes: Requires parts to have part references (AMPARTREF) or standard parts data.

tools.name: AMBOM
tools.description: AutoCAD Mechanical command that opens the BOM (bill of materials) dialog for editing the drawing's BOM database: items, quantities, part numbers and descriptions, merging and sorting rows.
tools.usage: AMBOM

parameters.name: BOM table
parameters.description: Data that drives balloons and parts lists (AMPARTLIST).

tools.example:
AMBOM
<edit description of item 3, sort by item number>
tools.notes: The BOM can be exported to spreadsheets or databases for ERP systems.

tools.name: AMPARTREF
tools.description: AutoCAD Mechanical command that attaches a part reference (part data such as name, number, material, vendor) to geometry so that it appears in the BOM and can be ballooned.
tools.usage:
AMPARTREF
Specify location
Part Reference dialog

parameters.name: part data
parameters.description: Description, standard, material, part number and custom properties.

tools.example:
AMPARTREF
<pick on bracket>
<enter PART NUMBER BRK-120, material S235>
tools.notes: Standard parts inserted from the content library carry their data automatically.

tools.name: AutoCAD Map 3D toolset
tools.description: GIS and mapping toolset combining CAD and GIS data: FDO connections to spatial databases and files, coordinate systems and transformations, attached source drawings with queries, object data, topology, drawing cleanup, thematic mapping and annotation.
tools.usage:
Start the 'AutoCAD Map 3D 2025' shortcut
Key commands: MAPIMPORT, MAPEXPORT, ADESETCRDSYS, MAPCONNECT, ADEQUERY, ADEDEFDATA, MAPCLEAN

parameters.name: FDO providers
parameters.description: SHP, SDF, SQLite, Oracle, SQL Server spatial, WMS/WFS, raster and more.

parameters.name: Task Pane
parameters.description: MAPWSPACE shows Display Manager, Map Explorer and Map Book.

tools.example: ADESETCRDSYS (assign UTM84-32N) -> MAPCONNECT (connect to parcels.shp) -> style layers in Display Manager -> MAPEXPORT
tools.notes: Data brought in with MAPCONNECT stays linked to the source; MAPIMPORT converts features into drawing objects. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: MAPIMPORT
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D command that imports external GIS files into the drawing as AutoCAD objects, bringing attributes in as object data or links and optionally applying display settings and a coordinate transformation.
tools.usage:
MAPIMPORT
choose format and file > Import dialog: layer mapping, data (object data / link template), coordinate system

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ESRI Shapefile, MapInfo MIF/TAB, ArcInfo coverages/E00, SDF, GML, MicroStation DGN and others.

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: Create object data from attributes or link to a database.

parameters.name: Coordinate conversion
parameters.description: Transform from the file's coordinate system to the drawing's.

tools.example:
ADESETCRDSYS (set drawing coordinate system first)
MAPIMPORT
<ESRI Shapefile> C:\GIS\parcels.shp
<Data: Create object data> OK
tools.notes: Points with elevations and mismatched coordinate systems are the usual sources of 'data in the wrong place'; set the drawing's coordinate system before importing.

tools.name: MAPEXPORT
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D command that exports drawing objects and their object data or linked data to GIS formats such as SHP, MIF/TAB, SDF, GML or DGN, with filters, data mapping and coordinate conversion.
tools.usage:
MAPEXPORT
choose format and file > Export dialog: Selection, Data, Options

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Objects or layers to export (a shapefile holds one geometry type).

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: Map object data, links and properties to attribute fields.

tools.example:
MAPEXPORT
<ESRI Shapefile> C:\GIS\out\pipes.shp
<Selection: layer W-PIPE, Data: object data table PIPES>
tools.notes: Closed polylines export as polygons; set that option explicitly for area features.

tools.name: ADESETCRDSYS
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D command that assigns a global coordinate system code to the current drawing, which is required for transforming data between coordinate systems when attaching drawings, connecting FDO sources, importing and exporting.
tools.usage:
ADESETCRDSYS
Coordinate System - Assign dialog: search by code, category or EPSG

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Coordinate system code such as LL84 or UTM84-32N (EPSG searchable).

tools.example:
ADESETCRDSYS
<search 'UTM84-32N'> Assign
tools.notes: Assigning a coordinate system does not move existing geometry; it declares what the coordinates mean. Plain AutoCAD's GEOGRAPHICLOCATION uses a compatible coordinate library.

tools.name: MAPCONNECT
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D command that opens Data Connect to connect to a feature source through an FDO provider (files, spatial databases, web services, rasters) and add its feature classes as layers in the Display Manager.
tools.usage:
MAPCONNECT
Data Connect: choose provider > set connection parameters > Connect > Add to Map

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: SHP, SDF, SQLite, Oracle, SQL Server Spatial, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, WMS, WFS, raster ...

parameters.name: feature classes
parameters.description: Tables/layers chosen for display.

tools.example:
MAPCONNECT
<Add SHP Connection> folder C:\GIS\city\ > Connect > Add to Map
tools.notes: Edits to connected features require check-out/check-in (MAPCHECKOUT, MAPCHECKIN) depending on the provider.

tools.name: ADEQUERY
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D command that defines, saves, loads and executes queries against attached source drawings, retrieving objects by location, property, object data or SQL conditions in Preview, Draw or Report mode.
tools.usage:
ADEQUERY
Define Query of Attached Drawing(s) dialog: Location / Property / Data / SQL conditions, Query mode

parameters.name: Location
parameters.description: All, window, polygon, buffer fence or boundary.

parameters.name: Query mode
parameters.description: Preview (temporary), Draw (bring objects into the drawing) or Report (write to file).

tools.example:
ADEQUERY
Location: Window around project area
Property: Layer = W-*
Mode: Draw > Execute Query
tools.notes: Attached drawings are managed with ADEDRAWINGS; query results can be saved back to source drawings.

tools.name: ADEDEFDATA
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D command that defines object data tables (named field lists with types) stored in the drawing, which are then attached to objects with ADEATTACHDATA to hold attributes like pipe material or inspection date.
tools.usage:
ADEDEFDATA
Define Object Data dialog: table name, fields (Character, Integer, Real, Point)

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Object data table name.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Field name, type and default value.

tools.example:
ADEDEFDATA
Table PIPES: MATERIAL (Character), DIAMETER (Integer), YEAR (Integer)
ADEATTACHDATA
<select pipes>
tools.notes: Object data travels with the drawing; MAPEXPORT can write it to GIS attribute fields.

tools.name: MAPCLEAN
tools.description: AutoCAD Map 3D drawing-cleanup command that corrects digitizing and conversion errors: deleting duplicates, erasing short objects, breaking crossing objects, extending undershoots, snapping clustered nodes, dissolving pseudo-nodes and more, usually as a preparation for topology.
tools.usage:
MAPCLEAN
Drawing Cleanup dialog: Select objects > Select actions and tolerances > Cleanup methods (interactive or automatic)

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: Delete Duplicates, Erase Short Objects, Break Crossing Objects, Extend Undershoots, Snap Clustered Nodes, Dissolve Pseudo Nodes, Erase Dangling Objects, Simplify Objects ...

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Distance within which errors are fixed.

tools.example:
MAPCLEAN
<select parcel boundaries>
Actions: Delete Duplicates, Break Crossing Objects, Snap Clustered Nodes (tol 0.01)
Automatic > Finish
tools.notes: Save a copy first; automatic cleanup with large tolerances can distort geometry. Cleanup profiles can be saved and reused.

tools.name: AutoCAD Plant 3D toolset
tools.description: Process plant design toolset with P&ID drafting, spec-driven 3D piping, equipment and structural modelling, and automatic orthographic and isometric drawing production, all organised in Plant projects with a shared project database.
tools.usage:
Start the 'AutoCAD Plant 3D 2025' shortcut
Project Manager (PROJECTMANAGER) / Data Manager (DATAMANAGER)
Key commands: PLANTPIPEADD, PLANTORTHOCREATE, PLANTPRODUCTIONISO

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project.xml plus project databases (SQLite locally or SQL Server / Autodesk Docs collaboration).

parameters.name: specs
parameters.description: Piping specs created in the Spec Editor from catalogs.

tools.example: Create project > P&ID drawing > 3D model with PLANTPIPEADD > PLANTORTHOCREATE > PLANTPRODUCTIONISO
tools.notes: Plant drawings must be opened from within their project for data consistency. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: PLANTPIPEADD
tools.description: AutoCAD Plant 3D command that routes pipe using the current spec and size, inserting fittings (elbows, tees, reducers) from the spec automatically, with compass and routing tools for accurate placement.
tools.usage:
PLANTPIPEADD
Specify start point (current spec and size from the Home ribbon; command options for elevation and routing)
Specify next point ...

parameters.name: Spec / Size
parameters.description: Current pipe spec and nominal size (set on the Home ribbon).

parameters.name: Elevation
parameters.description: Routing elevation.

tools.example:
PLANTPIPEADD
<start at pump nozzle>
<route to vessel nozzle>
<Enter>
tools.notes: Start at equipment nozzles to keep connectivity; disconnected ends appear in validation.

tools.name: PLANTORTHOCREATE
tools.description: AutoCAD Plant 3D command that creates a new orthographic view (plan, elevation or section) of selected 3D model areas in an ortho drawing, with annotation that updates when the model changes.
tools.usage:
PLANTORTHOCREATE
Select reference models > define ortho cube > view direction and scale > place view

parameters.name: ortho cube
parameters.description: 3D box defining the region and view direction.

parameters.name: scale / display
parameters.description: View scale and hidden-line settings.

tools.example:
PLANTORTHOCREATE
<select pump area model> Top view 1:50 <place on sheet>
tools.notes: PLANTORTHOADJACENT creates related views; PLANTORTHOANNOTATE adds component annotations.

tools.name: PLANTPRODUCTIONISO
tools.description: AutoCAD Plant 3D command that generates production isometric drawings (and PCF data) for selected pipe lines using iso style settings, with bills of material, weld and cut lists.
tools.usage:
PLANTPRODUCTIONISO
select line numbers / iso style > Create

parameters.name: iso style
parameters.description: Layout, title block and annotation settings.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: Line numbers to generate.

tools.example:
PLANTPRODUCTIONISO
<select lines 100-P-001, 100-P-002> <Final_ANSI-B iso style> Create
tools.notes: PLANTQUICKISO produces check isos quickly without the full production settings.

tools.name: AutoCAD Raster Design toolset
tools.description: Raster editing and raster-to-vector toolset: insert and correlate scanned images and georeferenced rasters, clean and edit raster data, manipulate raster entities (REM) and convert scanned linework to vectors.
tools.usage:
Loaded into AutoCAD or toolsets (Raster Tools ribbon tab)
Key commands: IINSERT, IMATCH, VLINE

parameters.name: correlation
parameters.description: World files, GeoTIFF and manual matching position images.

parameters.name: REM
parameters.description: Raster entity manipulation of lines, arcs and regions as objects.

tools.example: IINSERT (scan.tif) -> IMATCH (align to survey points) -> IDESPECKLE (clean) -> VLINE (vectorize walls)
tools.notes: Images inserted with IINSERT are compatible with standard IMAGE objects. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: IINSERT
tools.description: AutoCAD Raster Design command that inserts an image (TIFF, GeoTIFF, JPEG, PNG, ECW, MrSID and other formats), optionally using correlation data from the file or a world file to place and scale it.
tools.usage:
IINSERT
Insert Image dialog: file, correlation source, insertion options

parameters.name: correlation source
parameters.description: Embedded georeference, world file or manual placement.

parameters.name: Quick Insert
parameters.description: Insert using existing correlation without further prompts.

tools.example:
IINSERT
C:\Scans\sheet12.tif  (Correlation: world file)
tools.notes: IWORLDOUT writes correlation data to a world file for other applications.

tools.name: IMATCH
tools.description: AutoCAD Raster Design command that aligns an image to other images or vector geometry by matching pairs of source and destination points, adjusting scale, rotation and position (and rubber-sheeting with more points).
tools.usage:
IMATCH
Select image
Pick source point, destination point (repeat for more pairs)

parameters.name: point pairs
parameters.description: Two pairs for scale/rotate/move; more for rubber-sheet corrections (see IRSHEET).

tools.example:
IMATCH
<select scanned plan>
<pick grid intersection A on image> <pick A in vector grid>
<pick grid intersection B on image> <pick B in vector grid>
tools.notes: Choose widely separated points for accuracy.

tools.name: VLINE
tools.description: AutoCAD Raster Design vectorization command that converts raster lines into vector lines or polylines by picking along the raster linework, optionally removing the underlying raster pixels.
tools.usage:
VLINE
Pick raster line / follow prompts to trace segments

parameters.name: remove raster
parameters.description: Option to erase the traced pixels after vectorization.

tools.example:
VLINE
<pick along a scanned wall line>
<Enter>
tools.notes: VPLINE, VARC, VCIRCLE, VTEXT and VFPLINE vectorize polylines, arcs, circles, text and followed polylines.

tools.name: AutoCAD LT
tools.description: Lower-cost 2D drafting and documentation edition of AutoCAD that reads and writes the same DWG format. It lacks 3D modelling and rendering, Express Tools, the Action Recorder, Data Extraction, creation of parametric constraints, industry toolsets and the .NET, ObjectARX, VBA and COM automation APIs; AutoLISP is supported from AutoCAD LT 2024 with limitations.
tools.usage: AutoCAD LT 2024+: APPLOAD / (load "file.lsp") for AutoLISP, LSP/FAS/VLX and DCL files

parameters.name: AutoLISP in LT
parameters.description: Most vl-, vla-, vlax- and vlr- functions work; no external COM objects (vlax-create-object, vlax-get-object, vlax-get-or-create-object, vlax-import-type-library, GetInterfaceObject).

parameters.name: 3D
parameters.description: 3D models can be viewed and moved/copied/deleted but not created or edited.

parameters.name: no VLIDE
parameters.description: The Visual LISP IDE is not available; edit code with VS Code or another editor.

tools.example:
; LT-safe routine: uses only core AutoLISP and ActiveX on the drawing itself
(defun c:LAYFIX () (vl-load-com)
  (vlax-for l (vla-get-Layers (vla-get-ActiveDocument (vlax-get-acad-object)))
    (vla-put-Lock l :vlax-false))
  (princ))
tools.notes: entmake/entmod can only create objects that LT supports; functions exposed by ObjectARX or .NET applications are unavailable. Drawings with 3D solids or toolset objects remain intact when edited in LT.

tools.name: AutoCAD web app
tools.description: Browser-based AutoCAD (web.autocad.com) for viewing, editing and creating 2D drawings from any computer, with drawings stored in Autodesk Docs/Drive or connected cloud storage. It covers core 2D drafting, editing, blocks, layers and measuring, and runs basic AutoLISP routines from .lsp files.
tools.usage:
https://web.autocad.com  > open DWG from Autodesk Docs, Autodesk Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box or Google Drive
LISP tab > Manage LISP (upload .lsp, choose startup files)

parameters.name: LISP support
parameters.description: Only .lsp files (no FAS/VLX); requires an AutoCAD subscription; routines calling unavailable features fail.

parameters.name: no 3D / APIs
parameters.description: No 3D modelling, .NET, ObjectARX, VBA or DCL dialogs.

tools.example: LISP tab > Manage LISP > upload acme_basic.lsp > set as startup > run ACMEREV at the command line
tools.notes: Good for quick edits and markups away from the office; heavy customization should stay on desktop AutoCAD. SAVETOWEBMOBILE on the desktop pushes drawings to the web/mobile storage.

tools.name: AutoCAD mobile app
tools.description: iOS and Android app for viewing, measuring, marking up and making simple 2D edits to DWG files on phones and tablets, including offline access to downloaded drawings and cloud storage integration.
tools.usage: Install 'AutoCAD - DWG Viewer & Editor' from the app store > sign in with an Autodesk ID > open drawings from device or cloud storage

parameters.name: tools
parameters.description: Viewing, layers, measure, markup, basic draw/edit (feature depth depends on subscription).

parameters.name: offline
parameters.description: Drawings can be made available offline and synchronized later.

tools.example: Open site_plan.dwg on a tablet > Measure distance > Add markup cloud with note > Save back to Autodesk Docs
tools.notes: No LISP or programming support; intended for field review rather than production drafting.
